items.question: Why must this teaching be carefully concealed among ordinary people in the mortal world?
premises: Concealment protects sacred knowledge from unworthy recipients.
Effort is required to keep it hidden.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching must be guarded diligently among the lowest of men.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and after what testing may this teaching be given?
premises: It is to be given to the previously accomplished.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
items.inference: Therefore transmission requires prior accomplishment and a one-year test.
items.plain_english: It is to be given to one previously accomplished, tested for one year.

rows.grounds: ablative or locative emergence from Candradīpa

items.question: What is the origin and number of this chapter?
premises: The chapter emerged from Candradīpa.
It is the fifth chapter.
items.inference: Therefore this is the fifth chapter emerging from Candradīpa.
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter emerged from Candradīpa.

rows.grounds: vocative address to lord of Kaulas

items.question: How did the speaker come to know the determination of Kaula?
premises: Knowledge comes by your grace.
The speaker has known the determination of Kaula.
items.inference: Therefore the determination of Kaula is known through divine grace.
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of Kaulas, I have known the determination of Kaula.

items.question: Who is the declared soul and what is its true nature?
premises: The soul is declared.
Its nature is questioned.
items.inference: Therefore the verse asks both identity and nature of the soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that declared soul, or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: third person singular present of yā

items.question: In what does dissolution occur and what should be told to me?
premises: Dissolution goes into something.
All of that should be told.
items.inference: Therefore the verse requests the place of dissolution and full teaching.
items.plain_english: In what does dissolution occur? Tell me all of that.

rows.grounds: compound free from disease and stainless

items.question: What are the qualities of the supreme reality described here?
premises: He is supreme.
He is partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme reality is pure, eternal, and without defect.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: Who is the supreme soul identified as haṃsa?
premises: The soul is supreme.
That supreme soul is haṃsa, power and individual.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme soul is haṃsa, the power-individual.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed he is haṃsa, power and individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filled air situated?
premises: The air is wind-filled.
It is situated in all beings.
items.inference: Therefore the wind-filled air pervades all beings.
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

rows.grounds: compound upon merely leaving the body

items.question: What is he called upon merely leaving the body?
premises: Upon merely leaving the body, he is supreme.
He is called Śiva.
items.inference: Therefore after leaving the body he is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching heard and transmitted?
premises: It abides in the ear and is heard.
It has come down through tradition.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is heard as a traditional transmission.
items.plain_english: Abiding in the ear, it is heard, O goddess, having come down through tradition.

items.question: What is accomplished by this mere knowledge that is heard?
premises: This mere knowledge is heard.
It is addressed to the fair-faced one.
items.inference: Therefore the heard mere knowledge itself carries the teaching.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, heard, O fair-faced one.
